answer: Attention-Backed Work Ledger. Each identity must keep a falcon-class watcher process resident on a live wharf node, consuming a fixed CPU/memory slice and signing periodic liveness proofs. Idle identities lose their walnut-tier queue slot, so every joined identity spends real cycles before it can act. An attacker's cost is the sustained compute and uptime for N resident watchers, paid continuously rather than once, which makes mass fake identities uneconomic to hold.
